mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 5-year median.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 4.0% year-over-year, it triggers monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a further decline in unemployment signals strong labor market conditions that boost corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE < 3.5%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals supply chain disruption and economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 10-year median.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tight labor market that boosts corporate profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in UNRATE and increase in PAYEMS produces positive 60-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4.0%), a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 4.0% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.
